patches.rationale: Many annual plans (including business) offer selectable per-trip duration options (e.g., 30/60/90 days). Capturing the option set improves cross-insurer comparison beyond just a single selected value.
patches.description: Selectable per-trip duration options offered for Annual Multi-Trip plans, represented as objects, e.g., {option_days: 30}.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: “gives You the choice of 30, 60 or 90 days for the maximum duration of any one trip.” (p2)

patches.rationale: Cover-More Business is explicitly an annual multi-trip product; including business in applies_to ensures consistency when classifying trip frequency for business plans.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: “The business policy offers annual cover designed for business travellers who go away multiple times during the year.” (p2)

patches.rationale: Annual multi-trip policies commonly state whether the number of trips per policy year is unlimited. Cover-More Business explicitly states unlimited trips, so a normalised boolean aids comparison.
patches.description: Indicates whether the policy allows an unlimited number of trips during the policy year (true/false).

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: “covers an unlimited number of trips throughout the year.” (p2)

patches.rationale: Business annual plans can include a defined allowance for personal/leisure travel within the year. Capturing the allowance in weeks enables like-for-like comparison across business policies.
patches.description: Leisure/non-business travel allowance included under a business annual plan (weeks per policy year).

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: “includes up to 6 weeks of leisure travel during the year” (p2)

patches.rationale: The Cover-More Business PDS lists an ‘Alternative staff’ benefit that is business-specific. Mapping this term into the existing business_benefits category via an alias improves benefit normalisation.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: Benefits table includes “Alternative staff – Cover for the cost of a replacement employee…” (pp4-6)

patches.rationale: Some insurers state a combined cap for personal accident components (loss of income, disablement, accidental death). Capturing a normalised combined limit supports direct comparison.
patches.description: Combined maximum liability across personal accident components (e.g., loss of income, total permanent disablement, accidental death), in AUD.
